_about: Public-domain Daniel Denison Whedon (1808-1885), Methodist Episcopal theologian and editor of the Methodist Quarterly Review, for the Word Hoard: Public Addresses (1852), The Freedom of the Will (1864), What is Arminianism? (1879), Statements Theological and Critical (1887) and Essays, Reviews and Discourses (1887), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 52 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

whedon-public-addresses: Public addresses, collegiate and popular (Boston : J.P. Jewett, 1852)
whedon-freedom-of-will: The freedom of the will as a basis of human responsibility and a divine government : elucidated and maintained in its issue with the necessitarian theories of Hobbes, Edwards, the Princeton essayists, and other leading advocates (New York : Nelson & Phillips, 1864)
whedon-arminianism: What is Arminianism? : with a brief sketch of Arminius (Toronto : William Briggs, 1879)
whedon-statements: Statements, theological and critical (New York : Phillips & Hunt ; Cincinnati : Cranston & Stowe, 1887)
whedon-essays: Essays, reviews, and discourses (New York, Phillips & Hunt, 1887)

_excluded.whedon-other: His Commentary on the New Testament and Old Testament (1860-1880s, many volumes) left for a later round; Letter to Dr. Stevens (1859, a pamphlet); Cox's Letters on the Second Coming (another author)
